sec: Normal GFR & its clinical use · p734

items.q: The lower limit of the normal GFR range printed on this page is:
A 52-year-old with a GFR of 13 ml/min has nausea, pericardial rub and an uraemic rash. Applying this page's use of GFR, the patient is in:
opts: G5 / end-stage renal disease, the uremic phase — dialysis required
G4 CKD, where erythropoietin alone is the listed step
G3a CKD, where cystatin C must confirm before any decision
Not classifiable, since the page classifies only by creatinine
items.exp: The page's single worked use of GFR is CKD classification: GFR <15 ml/min = G5/ESRD/uremic phase, dialysis required. (Book p734)

items.q: As printed on this page, GFR is used both to stage acute kidney injury and to classify chronic kidney disease.
opts: False — only CKD classification is stated here
True — AKI stages are listed beside the G5 line
True — but only when the UF coefficient is normal
False — the page says GFR has no staging role
items.exp: The 'Use' line states that chronic kidney disease (CKD) is classified based on GFR; no AKI staging appears on this page. (Book p734)

items.q: Every one of these is a threshold or use stated on this page EXCEPT:
opts: GFR <30 ml/min marks the uremic phase requiring dialysis
CKD is classified on the basis of GFR
items.exp: The dialysis-requiring uremic cut-off printed here is <15 ml/min; 30 ml/min is not the figure on this page. (Book p734)
